subject: SOC 2 renewal: evidence rollout, retention and capacity uplift
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@pioneerfin.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@pioneerfin.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 renewal window + throughput ask for renewal discussions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for walking us through the renewal packet last week. As we start our procurement cadence I wanted to outline two critical asks from Pioneer before we route the amendment to our procurement and legal teams:

1) Retention window: we need to move from 90 days to 18 months for audit logs tied to the product instance for our payments workload.
2) Evidence cadence: given an upcoming internal audit, Pioneer needs staged delivery of SOC 2 evidence (controls runbook, change logs, and the last 12 months of security events) in three deliveries over 6 weeks.
3) Capacity uplift: pilot to increase throughput for a new payments feature (target peak +35% tokens) for Q1 — we need pricing and a short pilot plan.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support the 18 month retention as an amendment, whether we can do a staged evidence delivery (please confirm file formats and access methods), and whether there is capacity headroom for a 30–40% short-term uplift with a pilot? If you can share a mutual action plan (MAP) and a redline we can circulate internally, that would speed things up.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is targeting an internal decision by mid-December.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Compliance, Pioneer Financial
Olivia Barnes | Pioneer Financial

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@pioneerfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal window + throughput ask for renewal discussions

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear outline. Confirming receipt and looping in Kimberly (legal/contracts) and Vanessa (Customer Success / renewals) to coordinate the amendment and staged evidence handoff. High level responses below and an attached MAP + evidence checklist.

- Retention window: We can offer an 18-month audit log retention amendment. There are two implementation choices: 1) stretched retention on our hosted stack (adds storage and retrieval SLA); or 2) deliver a time-bound evidence export bundle (encrypted, in-region) with an agreed retrieval SLA. We'll enumerate both in the amendment redline.
- Staged evidence delivery: Agreed. We'll provide the evidence in three batches (Controls runbook + configuration export; change log + RBAC snapshots; rolling security events for last 12 months). Preferred transfer is a secured Drive share + SFTP option for bulk manifests.
- Capacity pilot: We can run a 30–40% pilot for 4 weeks. Pricing for the pilot and the permanent uplift are in the attached MAP (worksheet tab: pricing scenarios). For the pilot we recommend: dedicated burst nodes, a KV-cache warmup window, and a short A/B routing policy to ensure stability.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Kimberly to issue the redline amendment that captures retention method + retrieval SLA + cost impact (we'll include a one-time credit for the pilot).
2) I will schedule a short technical sync (30m) with Pioneer infra to agree transfer formats and the pilot onboarding runbook.
3) Once Pioneer confirms the MAP and redline, Vanessa will coordinate signature and billing adjustments.

Attached: MAP_v1.3.xlsx (mutual action plan), SOC2_evidence-checklist.pdf

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Hi Olivia & team,

Thanks — attaching the first-pass redline (redline_amendment.docx). Key items to note from Legal: 

- Retention approach: we prefer the "export bundle with retrieval SLA" for hosted customers to avoid changing base retention for all tenants. The amendment contains both options; please mark which you prefer.
- Retrieval SLA (if export bundle chosen): 5 business days for a complete evidence bundle; expedited (2 business days) available as a billable add-on.
- Audit log format & checksum: The export will be delivered as gzipped JSONL with SHA256 checksums and an index file. Please confirm Pioneer can accept that format or if SFTP with CSV slices is required.
- Pricing & credits: Legal approved a one-time credit equivalent to 20% of the first-month uplift for the pilot if Pioneer signs amendment by Dec 20. The MAP has pricing bands for 30% and 40% throughput increases.

Questions for Pioneer (Legal Ops):
1) Do you confirm acceptance of JSONL gzipped exports with checksums?
2) Which retention implementation do you prefer (stretched retention vs export bundle)?
3) Any internal constraints on exports landing in a cloud region (we can do us-west only or multi-region)?

I'll stand by to incorporate your feedback and produce a DocuSign-ready amendment once we lock the retention method.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Hi Kimberly / Mateo — thanks for the quick turnaround and the MAP. We discussed this with Legal Ops and the infra team — answers below and a couple of requests: 

- Export format: Pioneer accepts gzipped JSONL with SHA256 checksums. We'll ingest via SFTP. Please include a sample file in the first delivery so our ingestion pipeline can validate.
- Retention implementation: Pioneer prefers the export-bundle approach (option 2) but wants the retrieval SLA at 2 business days for the first 12 months (we'll accept the billable add-on).
- Region: us-west is fine.
- Pilot: we accept the 4-week pilot for +35% throughput. Please confirm exact node counts and an expected start date in January.
- DocuSign: can Redwood produce a DocuSign-ready amendment once you incorporate our retrieval SLA change? We will route immediately.

Action items for Redwood: include a sample gzipped JSONL file in batch 1, produce the DocuSign amendment with the expedited retrieval SLA and the pilot credit. We can sign the amendment as soon as we see the DocuSign link — procurement remains on a mid-December decision path.
